candidate.blueprint_topic: Health Promotion and Maintenance — age-related vital-sign expectations
candidate.educational_objective: Recognize the normal age-related trend in resting heart rate from infancy to adulthood.

options.A: Resting heart rate is generally lowest in infancy and rises with age
options.B: Resting heart rate remains essentially unchanged from infancy through adulthood
options.C: Resting heart rate is generally higher in infants and decreases toward adult ranges with age
options.D: Healthy adults generally have higher resting heart rates than infants

candidate.rationale: Age-specific pediatric vital-sign tables show higher expected heart-rate ranges in newborns and infants than in older children, adolescents, and adults. The expected resting range narrows downward as children mature. C is correct.
candidate.source_claim_supported: Expected resting heart-rate ranges are generally higher in infants and decrease with age toward adolescent/adult ranges.
candidate.source_document_title: Nursing Health Promotion — Table 14.5b Heart Rate Ranges by Age; Treating Arrhythmias in Children
